understanding.emotion: tired of failing and not knowing why

understanding.week_thesis: The thing you keep failing at is not the problem. The loop of trying without a clear next step is. This week is about breaking that loop with one small, clear move.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verse.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
verse.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
verse.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
verse.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in the middle of the battlefield, his body heavy with doubt. They have been trying to build these apps for years, and the failures have worn them down to the bone. They ask Krishna what becomes of someone who believes, tries, slips, and does not make it to the end. Krishna answers that no sincere effort is ever wasted, and what you have already done carries forward into your next attempt.
verse.for_you: The years of trying have not vanished. They are still there, waiting under the surface. You do not need to find a new reason to begin, only to see the ground you have already covered.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him that the result of every action is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some do not. But those who never try never succeed at all. The failure of the apps is not the end. The loop of trying without a clear next step is the real failure. The days slipping by are the proof of the loop, not of your inability.
verse.for_you: You have tried many times to build these apps. The results were uncertain, and you did not succeed. But you never stopped trying. That refusal to stop is the one thing that has not failed, even when the apps did.

verse.speaker: Narrator
verse.setting: Angad plants his foot in Ravana's court and dares anyone to move it; no one can.
verse.sanskrit: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
verse.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.translation: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.why: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

prasang.title: Angad in Ravana's court
prasang.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
prasang.story_hook: Angad sat down in the enemy's court, and they began to insult his father.
prasang.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

verse.meaning: Angad stands in Ravana's court, his foot planted on the ground. Ravana has insulted him, but Angad holds his place. His foot does not move, and the pride of the enemy drains away. A steady mind does not leave what is right, though a million obstacles come. It is not about winning the argument right now. It is about staying in the place you chose, letting the noise of the court pass you by while your own purpose remains fixed.
verse.for_you: You are tired of the failure, but the app is not the real thing you are holding. The real thing is the part of you that still knows building is right. Let that part of you stand still today, while the doubt and the noise move around it. Just keep the foot planted.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: यो यमर्थं प्रार्थयते तदर्थं चेहते क्रमात् । अवश्यं स तमाप्नोति न चेदर्धान्निवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Want it, work for it step by step, and you will get there, unless you quit halfway.
verse.translation: Whoever wants something and works for it step by step will surely get it, unless they turn back halfway.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.
verse.misuse: Effort shapes results, but not every outcome is yours to control; see 2.6.21.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is speaking to the young Rama, who has just seen his father die and fears a world without justice. The teacher tells him that fate is not a fixed thing handed down from above. It is only the fruit of past effort. A person who wants something and works for it step by step will surely get it, unless they turn back halfway. The past is not a prison. Today's effort is the seed of tomorrow. Do not grieve what was never in your hands. The only real failure is to stop halfway.
verse.for_you: The loop of trying without a clear next step is what has you stuck. Break it today by choosing one small, concrete step for one of your apps and finishing it. Let the rest wait. Your past effort shaped this moment, but your present effort shapes what comes next.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on effort and grace, after Prahlada's story.
verse.sanskrit: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥
verse.line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
verse.translation: Through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness.
verse.why: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

prasang.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
prasang.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to Rama after Prahlada's awakening. He says that through daily practice and clear thinking, the mind becomes clear slowly, just as a mango ripens into its sweetness. The mind does not ripen in a single burst of effort. It ripens through steady, daily work, and through grace that meets that work. The mind is like the fruit. It needs time and consistent care to become sweet.
verse.for_you: Your project is not a mango that is already rotten. It is a fruit that simply needs the daily warmth of one small step to ripen. Today, do one clear, tiny part of the app and let the rest of the tree wait.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.hook_title: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.teaser: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.for_you: You have the skills and the years of effort. You know how to build. The hesitation right now is not a lack of ability. It is a holding back that can be let go of, just as Hanuman let go of his doubt at the shore.

script: You are tired of failing and not knowing why. The years of trying to build these apps have left you wondering if every attempt was just a waste of time.
Arjuna stands in the middle of the battlefield, his body heavy with doubt. They have been trying to build these apps for years, and the failures have worn them down to the bone. Arjuna said:
अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः, अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति.
In plain words: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?

Krishna tells them that a sincere effort is never wasted. The progress you make is not erased by a fall. It remains inside you as a foundation for the next step. This is easier said than done because the mind quickly turns failure into proof that you cannot succeed, making the next attempt feel impossible before it begins.

Look at the ground you have already covered. You do not need to find a new reason to begin, only to see the work you have already done. Let that be the reason to take one small, clear step forward today.

depth.life: You are sitting with the phone in your hand, the weight of years of failed apps pressing on you. The children are asleep and your parents need you, but your mind is stuck on the loop of trying and failing. You do not know why you cannot move forward.
depth.points: Krishna is telling Arjuna that a sincere attempt is never erased. The effort you put in years ago is not a dead thing. It is a seed that has already taken root and will grow again when you return to it. The slip is not the end of the path.
depth.practice: Look at one line of code or one sketch you made months ago. Read it without judgment and see what it still holds.
depth.question: What if the failure was not a wall, but a door you have already walked through?
